requirement: Build a scikit-learn classifier for a customer table with numeric and categorical columns, some missing, where all imputation, scaling and encoding is learned inside the pipeline.
skeleton: Column lists and a build_model function returning a Pipeline of a ColumnTransformer with numeric and categorical sub-pipelines followed by LogisticRegression.
caption: A scikit-learn model for a table mixing numeric and categorical columns, with every preprocessing step fitted inside one Pipeline. build_model(*, c=1.0) builds a numeric Pipeline of SimpleImputer with the median then StandardScaler for age and income, and a categorical Pipeline of SimpleImputer with the most frequent value then OneHotEncoder with handle_unknown set to ignore for plan and country. A ColumnTransformer applies them as num and cat with remainder drop, so extra columns such as an id are discarded, and the final Pipeline chains it as pre with LogisticRegression as clf using C equal to c and max_iter 1000. The fixture asserts, on a pandas frame with gaps, that the model fits despite missing values and a string id column, that the numeric imputer learned the median and scaling centres the training data, that missing plans become the most frequent category, that an unseen country predicts without error, and that c reaches the classifier.

plan.intent: Predict churn from a mixed customer table
constraints: Numeric gaps are imputed with the median and then standardized
Categorical gaps take the most frequent value before one-hot encoding
Unknown categories at predict time are ignored
The c argument sets LogisticRegression C

rationale.teaches: Compose ColumnTransformer and nested Pipelines so each column type gets its own imputation and encoding, all fitted on training data only.
rationale.why: Preprocessing outside the pipeline leaks test statistics, strict encoders crash on new categories in production, and passthrough columns leak identifiers into the model.

ops.docstring: A leak-free mixed-type classification pipeline built on ColumnTransformer.

candidates.why_wrong: A category never seen in training raises ValueError at predict time.
Numeric gaps are filled with the mean instead of the robust median.
The string id column is passed through to the classifier and breaks fitting.
Missing plans become their own NaN category instead of the most frequent value.
The c argument is ignored so regularization strength cannot be tuned.
